hypotheses.justification:
`Config` is a `structure ... : Prop` whose fields (`Setup G D`, `Group.IsSolvable`, `thirdK`, `IsTriangle`, etc.) never mention `Finite G`. Section instance variables are dropped from structures when unused. Other theorems about `Config`, for example `K₁_le_X` in O4FibresConfig.lean, are stated with `omit [Finite G] in`, which confirms this. So the statement `z ∉ K₁` elaborates and is true without `[Finite G]`.

The proof does not need finiteness either. It only uses `hQ.z_facts` to get `z ≠ 1`. `z_facts` sits under `[Finite G]` in FourEightBase.lean, but its first components come from `Asc72.IsTriangle.third_kind hQ.setup.oddT hQ.setup.normal hQ.tri hn hord`. That lemma has no `[Finite G]` argument, because the `variable` line in Asc72Triangle.lean has none, and `hQ.setup` is a `Setup`, which does not need `Finite G` either. So after `obtain ⟨n, hn, -, hord, rfl⟩ := hQ.third`, the same `third_kind` call gives `hz1 : (u*v*w)^n ≠ 1`, i.e. `z ≠ 1`.

The rest of the proof uses `K₁_A5`, `K₁_comm`, `alternatingGroup.center_eq_bot` on `Fin 5`, and `MulEquiv.map_eq_one_iff`. None of these use `Finite G`. Deleting it, for example with `omit [Finite G] in`, only requires replacing the `z_facts` call by the `third_kind` call.
